title: KRUPS Precision Electric Coffee Grinders: 3 oz Capacity, 200W Motor, Stainless Steel Blades for Uniform Grinding of Coffee Beans, Herbs, Nuts, and Spice Grinder (Black)
description:
About this item
Versatile grinding: 200W motor and stainless steel blades efficiently grind coffee beans, spices, herbs, and nuts. Customize from coarse to fine for various brewing methods: cold brew, French press, drip, pour-over, and espresso.
Large capacity: 3 oz/85g bean hopper grinds enough for up to 12 cups of coffee. Perfect for preparing multiple servings or grinding larger quantities of spices for meal prep. Ideal for households, small offices, or entertaining guests.
One-touch operation: Simple and intuitive design allows for easy grinding with just one button. Press and hold to achieve desired grind consistency, ensuring precise control over your coffee or spice preparation.
Safety first: Lid-activated safety mechanism ensures blades only spin when the lid is securely in place. Provides peace of mind during operation, prevents accidental spills or injuries. Designed with user safety in mind, suitable for all households.
Compact design: Sleek and space-saving construction fits easily on countertops or in cabinets. The black finish complements various kitchen decors, making it a stylish addition to your culinary workspace.

reviews_5s:
This is the absolute best grinder I’ve ever used. I didn’t want to write a long drawn-out review, but it’s so useful I felt compelled to write something.

I always do a lot of research before buying anything. I’m definitely THAT guy. This made it on a short list of grinders after an absurd amount of time (literally hours) of researching and watching videos. It’s probably a sickness doing that thorough of research for a sub-$50 purchase, but I digress. After that research I pulled the trigger and bought this one, and couldn’t be happier I did. That was a little while ago, probably a year and a half, and I’ve bought multiple ones for my friends since.

This grinder has an extremely consistent grind and achieves that grind in literally seconds (not hyperbole whatsoever).

It has a reasonable capacity too. It’s not Marianna’s-Trench level of capacity like some, but it doesn’t feel like I’m grinding coffee for ants either like some others. It’s perfect for making a batch of brew.

It has held up very well under pretty hard and consistent use, with both my toddler son and me battering it to get coffee unpacked after a fine-grind.

It’s even easy to clean. I use a dry napkin, get the majority of the leftover, then just run the metal part under the sink on low. It fills up, I pour it out, wipe it down and botta boom botta bing, it’s like new.

Super simple, effective and straightforward kitchen tool.
Definitely get it. Use my research-sickness to your advantage and just get it.I've been using the KRUPS Precision Electric Coffee Grinder for about three months now, and it's become an essential part of my kitchen! While I primarily bought it for fresh coffee beans, I've discovered it works amazingly well for grinding tea leaves and various herbs for cooking too.

The power this compact machine packs is impressive - it reduces whole coffee beans to the perfect consistency in seconds, whether I want a fine espresso grind or something coarser for my French press. The precision settings actually deliver noticeable differences in grind size, which has helped me fine-tune my brewing process.

What I particularly love is how compact it is - it takes up minimal counter space in my small kitchen but performs like a much larger appliance. The sleek design looks great sitting out, and cleaning is surprisingly simple with the removable components.

For anyone looking for versatility beyond just coffee, this grinder handles dried herbs for cooking beautifully. I've used it for everything from grinding spices to creating my own tea blends. The sealed operation keeps all the aromatic oils contained until you're ready to use them.

This KRUPS grinder has definitely elevated my coffee experience while proving itself useful for multiple kitchen tasks!My coffee maker has a built in grinder, so for coffee beans, I had no need for a grinder. But when my cat started having problems eating her kibble, this product was perfect. It was clear that the cat had a dental problem and chewing became painful. The vet recommended smashing her kibble, but that was really inconvenient. I then tried grinding it my coffee maker's grinder, and that worked great, but I don't relish subtle tones of kitty kibble in my morning coffee, so I bought this. It worked perfectly. I would then mix the grind with a couple of tablespoons of water or the liquid from canned tuna, chicken, salmon, etc, and the cat loved it.

I have also used this grinder on the fresh rosemary and basil leaves. It works great, and is reasonably quiet and very easy clean. This was a great purchase.I bought this spice grinder a couple of months ago and I've used it almost every day, I've learned that it grinds better in bulk then in small quantities, it grinds every thing to a fine powder in large quantities which is great for soups seasoning and sauces that you want to keep smooth. But if you only put a little bit in it doesn't move around properly and spices get stuck under the blade I've also noticed it was very silent at first but after frequent use it has gotten louder, it's not super loud but it is definitely not silent anymore, it's not a problem for me but it might be for some people. Overall I love it and I would definitely recommend it. 👍I have had this coffee grinder for over 8 years now and I use it every single day, sometimes multiple times in a day. That is many 1000s of grinds without wearing out. This thing is durable! Those complaining that its hard to clean, just put 1/4 cup of uncooked rice in it and grind it to a powder, dump in the compost, hit it with a duster and vola, clean as a whistle! Operation couldn't be any simpler. Need a coarse grind, hold the button for a few seconds, need an espresso grind, hold for 30 seconds. Need a spice grinder? Buy a second one. They are cheap enough.

There is no reason to buy fancy expensive coffee grinders! Save that $$ for better beans!I use this product exclusively to grind spices. It was recommended by Pailin (Hot Thai Kitchen on YouTube) and this product works extremely well. It is not a professional grinder nor is it extremely potent, but it is more than enough for my needs at home any time I need to turn spices into power. Sometimes I do have to shake it and tilt it a bit in order to get everything pulverized, but for this price I cannot be more satisfied about this product. It looks good and doesn’t take much space at all and the powered spices are just right every time.I have had this for over a year now and it is used every morning. Great grinder, looks good enough to leave out and it is the most quiet I have heard. I can feed my cat morning breakfast and three feet away grind coffee. My buddy does not even flinch and sleepers down the hall are not disturbed.
Get some beans and grind your own. This is a very good way to go and the price is affordable.I have had this coffee grinder for about 2-1/2 years and it has been great. I use it maybe twice a week, and the process takes me about five minutes each time. Works great. Easy to use. Also, we have a grinder here at work (another brand) that stopped working and I purchased this Krups. I would highly recommend!To give people an idea of durability and reliability, we purchased our first one in 2004, and it lasted 10 years. We purchased a replacement in 2014, and that one is still going strong 11 years later at the time of this review. Unbelievable, simple coffee grinder that does its job for a long time.Great buy. It is not loud at all and like how fine the coffee can get and being able to control that.

The lid for the stainless steel bowl is great. I don't have to worry about where to store my coffee after ground.
reviews_1s:
PFAS are forever chemicals that are almost impossible to avoid but if your adding them to your coffee because the grinder you bought is made of PFAS then your mainlining toxic chemicals into your body through your coffee ritual.

I didn’t know Krups uses PFAS in their grinder until I bought this grinder (I had one from a number of years ago that stopped working but Ive been grinding my beans at the grocery store since then).

I contacted Krups through their online customer support re: this specific product using the serial numbers on the bottom. Their reply came late and confirmed PFAS comes into contact w the “water chamber” of what I assume to be another product of theirs, ie probably a coffee maker (not a grinder). OK cool!

Krups not only failed to address the question I had about this grinder but it and Amazon is complicit in directly adding PFAS into kitchen equipment that is coming directly into contact w food. Honestly, this is wild.

Bad bad bad on many levels. Shocked TBH.

Update: when I corrected them (Krups customer support) on the product they asked for a photo of the sticker label warning on the box. “Mngr said PFAS are not coming into contact w the coffee beans” I’m paraphrasing. WTH do I know. Nada. But I’m glad CA is doing something. Lots of chemicals in products CA is warning us on. Kudos to them. Krups on us yeeeshKrups is not worthy of even one star. This coffee bean grinder is satisfactory. We even purchased a second one when the first one stopped working. However, when we applied for a refund on the first because the product broke and was guaranteed for two years, Krups rejected our claim. They said Amazon was responsible for the refund. We spoke to an Amazon representative who initially said they were responsible for up to one year. Amazon later contacted us to say that because we were good customers, they would provide the refund. We told Krups and Amazon that we were rejecting Amazon's offer because Krups had guaranteed the product. We have not heard from Krups again.
In their email correspondence to us they close by saying: "Kind regards, Blessed, Krups Customer Service Advisor." We wonder who Krups considers Blessed, their untrustworthy selves or unsuspecting and trusting customer?It died after 5 uses. I should have read moe reviews before buying.
It was relatively quiet and did grind nicely when it did work.

As something I didn't use daily, it took me too long calendar wise to return it even with limited uses before death. There was no sign it was coming either- not a gradual wind down of quality or a noise that slowly got worse, just mirror going, blade not moving, and a bonus of instant "tired motor" smell that lead me to driving it to work with me for fear it would rebel and burn itself for a dramatic flare.

I kept it clean, dry, and stored when not in use but after going back over other reviews the sad truth seems to be this thing is simply a one trick pony that gives up quickly no matter what you do.Shame on me, for buying this product for the second time and wasting my money.

The first machine I bought in 2019 stopped working with smoke coming out from bottom of the unit. I used it grind small quantity of coffee (once every 3-4 weeks; the machine in total ran for ~ 2 minutes each use, with a 10 second cooling period for every 20 seconds of run time). The machine didn't last for more than 9 months.

I bought another unit from Amazon back in June 2020 and this one stopped working within 6 months, with the same exact issue (smoke from bottom of the unit).

I decided to reach out to KRUPS customer service this time and submitted a warranty ticket with them on 11/13/2020. In line with their product, KRUPS customer service is another example of how to drive away customers from a business. After patiently working with them for about 6 weeks, to get a replacement unit, I had finally given up. I WILL NEVER EVER do business with this company again!

Below is a summary of my interaction with KRUPS customer support - everything is via email and there is no way to talk to a live person (there is a customer service number posted on their website, but calling that number always plays a recorded message stating they are not able to take calls, due to Covid).

1. In response to a ticket I submitted on 11/13/20, I was asked by KRUPS on 11/25/20 to provide the proof of purchase / copy of my invoice, which I sent on the same day (11/25/20).

2. On 11/30/20, KRUPS customer service (Rick) asked me to send an image of the defective unit (with the power cord cut). I was asked to cut the power cord, take a picture of it & send it to them and was told a replacement order for a new grinder will be placed once I send the image. I sent the requested image on the same day (11/30/20).

3. On 12/1/20, I provided my shipping address to Rick, as requested. I also received a confirmation on the same day (12/1/20) that a replacement order for a new grinder was placed and that I will receive the new grinder in about 7 - 14 days.

4. It is 1/4/21 today.... which is more than a month since KRUPS customer service confirmed the replacement order was placed. However, I am yet to get the grinder. I sent several follow-up emails over the last 1 month - unfortunately there isn't a response as of yet.Once upon a time, the name Krups really stood out. It meant quality and dependability. I loved to have a Krups product, as I knew it would supply years of service, and it would meet exacting standards for my coffee experience.

No longer. This is the second grinder that has quit on me in the last 15 months, same model. The first was after about 2 years, and I had made the mistake of washing the grinding cup, so attributed that to my own poor treatment, even if simply endeavoring to do well.

Here, however, I have absolutely babied this grinder. I have treated it with care and according to all specs, and to have it quite on me after only a little over a year, that's simply unacceptable.

It is a real shame, also, as I love the grinder. It is one of the few that doesn't make me hate myself while it is running in the early morning, with a loud, clanging racket. Sadly, complete silence of a machine that has quit is not the alternative I was looking for.

Product support? Nope. Basically, fix it yourself. Literally, it instructs you to take it apart and lubricate the mechanism within. Seriously? Oh, with machine lubricant, for we all simply have that laying around, right?

Once, I would have sang the praises of this grinder, but now not only would I never recommend it, but would not recommend the Krups brand, either. Sad, to see once heralded leaders in manufacturing fall to lower performance standards than Walmart brands.Warning: the edge of the plastic lid wears away. You will get ground plastic in your coffee!

I've owned a couple of these for a long time, and it only recently dawned on me how badly the bottom edge of the clear plastic lid has eroded. The lid's vertical surface is ribbed, and between the rib there are now deep gaps, making the edge like a comb. This results from the whirling beans colliding with the plastic edge. Where did that plastic go? Reader, my wife and I drank it

In searching for a replacement yesterday, I noticed that some manufacturers, like Cuisinart and Bodum, now make their compact grinders so that the edge of the lid goes OUTSIDE a protective wall, keeping it away from the action, I assume for exactly this reason.

DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT.When I bought this Krups One-Touch Coffee and Spice Grinder, I imagined a sleek, futuristic device to transform my beans and spices into powdery perfection. What I got instead was a crash course in disappointment engineering.

Upon its first triumphant debut in my kitchen, I loaded it with fresh coffee beans, pressed the "One-Touch" button, and... poof! It emitted a faint whimper before deciding it had already lived its best life. The beans remained smugly whole, and I was left with a device that made a better paperweight than a grinder.

To its credit, it grinds expectations into dust—just not coffee.

The design is lovely, though. If you’re looking for an expensive way to decorate your counter or perhaps a novel conversation starter (“Hey, want to hear about the time my grinder gave up on life before it even started?”), this is your gadget. But for actual grinding? Unless you’re grinding your hopes and dreams, steer clear.

Krups, you’re on thin ice. Next time, I’ll take my chances with a mortar and pestle.

TL;DR: If you want a grinder that works just once and dies with flair, this is the one for you. Otherwise, save your money for something that doesn’t aspire to be a kitchen tragedy.The Lid goes inside the grinding apparatus, opposed to outside, which means coffee grounds get all over the counter when removing lid. Embarrassing that it would be engineered that way. If you don't use all of coffee ground and want to save it, you will have to put lid back on, which means the lid "seals" between grounds and plastic wall. One thing when it is whole beans for the lid to push out the way. Gound coffee means your getting even more on the counter when removing lid an additional time between grinding. Too many choices. Not worth the clean up at each use for this oneit is too delicate for human use. The lid is not designed well and ours broke in two from a single accidental drop. The design of the lid is that there is smaller lid within the outer lid to keep the grounds from spilling out. This interior lid looks like it was added as an afterthought in the design process and is not secured to the outer lid very well so that everyday use such as it slipping out of your hands means the end of it's life when the two are separated. We contacted Krups to see if it is under warranty but it is not.Worked great for the first 6 months. Silent vortex became less silent after 6 month, and after 8 months it started to sound more like a lawn mower. I tested it without removable grinding bowl, and the motor was very quite. Put it back and turned it on without coffee beans, and it was loud again. Called Krups, and they said that I need to send the unit to them for evaluation. I told them that I isolated the problem to the grinding bowl and they agreed to send new one to me. Two weeks later I received UPS from France with the part. Plugged it into the unit, turn it on and the sound was even louder. I sent email to Krups and explained the situation. In response they emailed me UPS label for return of the coffee grinder for evaluation and repair. I suggested that no company in the world can afford repair of $35 appliance and they should send me a new one and I return them old, but they refused. I gave up. Beware.
